question.worked_solution:
We recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{4!}-⋯-\frac{(-1)^{n}\,{x}^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{8}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}) & =1-\frac{{(\pi /8)}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{(\pi /8)}^{4}}{4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,{(\pi /8)}^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯ \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}) & =1-\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{{8}^{2}\cdot 2!}+\frac{{\pi }^{4}}{{8}^{4}\cdot 4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,{\pi }^{2n}}{{8}^{2n}\cdot (2n)!}+⋯ \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}) & =1-\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{64\cdot 2!}+\frac{{\pi }^{4}}{4\,096\cdot 4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,{\pi }^{2n}}{{8}^{2n}\cdot (2n)!}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the sum of the series is $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}).$
